Indications for use
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance the user's lower jaw and maintain this position during use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep. It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
Device Description
The L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is an intraoral device that is used to maintain the lower jaw in a forward position to increase pharyngeal space so as to improve the ability to exchange air and decrease air turbulence, a causative factor in snoring.
L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece includes three upper trays (A0, A2, A4) and three lower trays (B0, B1, B2). One upper tray and one lower tray are combined together for use. By randomly combining one upper tray with one lower tray, the device can be used for advancing lower jaw from 0mm to 6mm. 
Considering that the size of the oral cavity varies among different groups of people, L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to be available for two size (L and S). Even though the dimensions of these sizes of Anti Snoring Mouthpiece are different, by positioning the upper protrusion and the lower protrusion at different locations within the upper tray assembly and the lower tray assembly respectively, advancement distance of 0-6 mm can still be realized.

4. FIRST AID MEASURES 
Description of first aid measures 
Protection of first-aiders:  
First Aid responders should pay attention to self-protection and use the recommended protective 
clothing (chemical resistant gloves, splash protection).  If potential for exposure exists refer to Section 
8 for specific personal protective equipment.   
 
Inhalation: Move person to fresh air and keep comfortable for breathing; consult a physician.    
 
Skin contact: Seek first aid or medical attention as needed.  If molten material comes in contact with 
the skin, do not apply ice but cool under ice water or running stream of water. DO NOT attempt to

remove the material from skin. Removal could result in severe tissue damage.  Seek medical attention 
immediately.  Suitable emergency safety shower facility should be immediately available.   
 
Eye contact: Flush eyes thoroughly with water for several minutes.  Remove contact lenses after the 
initial 1-2 minutes and continue flushing for several additional minutes.  If effects occur, consult a 
physician, preferably an ophthalmologist.   
 
Ingestion: If swallowed, seek medical attention.  May cause gastrointestinal blockage.  Do not give 
laxatives.  Do not induce vomiting unless directed to do so by medical personnel.    
 
Most important symptoms and effects, both acute and delayed:  
Aside from the information found under Description of first aid measures (above) and Indication of 
immediate medical attention and special treatment needed (below), any additional important 
symptoms and effects are described in Section 11: Toxicology Information. 
 
Indication of any immediate medical attention and special treatment needed  
Notes to physician: If burn is present, treat as any thermal burn, after decontamination.  If lavage is 
performed, suggest endotracheal and/or esophageal control.  Danger from lung aspiration must be 
weighed against toxicity when considering emptying the stomach.  No specific antidote.  Treatment of 
exposure should be directed at the control of symptoms and the clinical condition of the patient.

6. ACCIDENTAL RELEASE MEASURES 
Personal precautions, protective equipment and emergency procedures: Spilled material may 
cause a slipping hazard.  Follow safe handling advice and personal protective equipment 
recommendations.   
 
Environmental precautions: Discharge into the environment must be avoided.  Prevent further 
leakage or spillage if safe to do so.  Retain and dispose of contaminated wash water.  Local 
authorities should be advised if significant spillages cannot be contained.   
 
Methods and materials for containment and cleaning up: Avoid dispersal of dust in the air (i.e., 
clearing dust surfaces with compressed air).  Dust deposits should not be allowed to accumulate on 
surfaces, as these may form an explosive mixture if they are released into the atmosphere in sufficient 
concentration.  Local or national regulations may apply to releases and disposal of this material, as 
well as those materials and items employed in the cleanup of releases. You will need to determine 
which regulations are applicable.  Sweep up spillage and collect in suitable container for disposal.   
See sections: 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13.   
 
7. HANDLING AND STORAGE 
Precautions for safe handling: Avoid breathing process fumes.  Do not breathe dust.  Minimize dust 
generation and accumulation.  Keep container closed when not in use.  Keep away from heat and 
sources of ignition.  Take precautionary measures against static discharges.  Use with adequate 
ventilation.  Take care to prevent spills, waste and minimize release to the environment.   Pneumatic 
conveying and other mechanical handling operations can generate combustible dust.  To reduce the 
potential for dust explosions, do not permit dust to accumulate.  Do not get molten material in eyes, on 
skin or clothing.  Handle in accordance with good industrial hygiene and safety practice.  
CONTAINERS MAY BE HAZARDOUS WHEN EMPTY.  Since emptied containers retain product 
residue follow all (M)SDS and label warnings evenafter container is emptied.   
Use only with adequate ventilation.  Static electricity may accumulate and ignite suspended dust 
causing an explosion.  Provide adequate precautions, such as electrical grounding and bonding, or 
inert atmospheres.   
 
Conditions for safe storage: Keep in properly labelled containers.  Store in accordance with the 
particular national regulations.   
 
Do not store with the following product types:  Strong oxidizing agents.   
Unsuitable materials for containers: None known.

Although some of the components of this product may have exposure guidelines, no exposure would 
be expected under normal handling conditions due to the physical state of the material.    
Exposure controls 
Engineering controls: Provide general and/or local exhaust ventilation to control airborne levels 
below the exposure guidelines.  Local exhaust ventilation is preferred for most operations.   
 
Individual protection measures 
Eye/face protection: Use safety glasses (with side shields).  If there is a potential for 
exposure to particles which could cause eye discomfort, wear chemical goggles.   If exposure 
causes eye discomfort, use a full-face respirator.   
Skin protection 
Hand protection: Chemical protective gloves should not be needed when handling 
this material. Consistent with general hygienic practice for any material, skin contact 
should be minimized.  Use gloves to protect from mechanical injury. Selection of 
gloves will depend on the task.  Use gloves with insulation for thermal protection, 
when needed.   
Other protection: No precautions other than clean body-covering clothing should be 
needed.   
Respiratory protection: Respiratory protection should be worn when there is a potential to 
exceed the exposure limit requirements or guidelines. If there are no applicable exposure limit 
requirements or guidelines, wear respiratory protection when adverse effects, such as 
respiratory irritation or discomfort have been experienced, or where indicated by your risk 
assessment process.  Use an approved air-purifying respirator when vapors are generated at 
increased temperatures or when dust or mist is present.   
The following should be effective types of air-purifying respirators:  When dust/mist are 
present use a/an  Particulate filter.  When combinations of vapors, acids, or dusts/mists are 
present use a/an  Organic vapor cartridge with a particulate pre-filter.

2. Model

4. Indication for use/Intended Use
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance the user's lower jaw and
maintain this position during use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep.
It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
5. Contraindications
Do not use the device if any of the following conditions apply:
1.Under 18 years of age, as it may affect the development of teeth and jawbones in
adolescents.
2.Diagnosed with Central Sleep Apnea (CSA), which differs from OSA.
3.Suffering from severe respiratory diseases, such as asthma, severe OSA, or
emphysema.
4.Experiencing periodontal disease, including loose teeth, gum bleeding, oral ulcers,
or cavities.
5.Having Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD) or other temporomandibular
joint issues.
6.Having had dental implants within the last 12 months.
7.Currently undergoing orthodontic treatment or wearing braces, full dentures, or
other dental appliances.
8.Having severe misalignment or bite issues (jaw or tooth pain when clenching).
6. Warnings
1. Use of the device may lead to:
1) Tooth movement or changes in bite
2) Gum or tooth soreness
3) Joint discomfort
4) Irritation inside the mouth
5) Excessive drooling
6) Obstructed mouth breathing
7) Dry mouth
2. If severe adverse reactions, allergies, breathing difficulties, or other respiratory
conditions occur, discontinue use of the device and consult a doctor immediately.
3. The device is not suitable for treating OSA.

7. Principles
Normal Breathing:
For normal person, adequate muscle tone in the throat and tongue keeps the airway
open.
Snoring
For snoring patients, they have muscle relaxation leading to partial airway obstruction.
Faster airflow through the narrow passage creates turbulence, causing tissue vibration.
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)
Complete relaxation of the muscles leads to total airway blockage, preventing airflow
and causing temporary breathing cessation.

By using the device, it can maintain the lower jaw in a forward position to increase
pharyngeal space so as to keep the airway open. Thus allowing for normal breathing.
8. Construction
L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece includes three upper trays (A0, A2, A4) and three
lower trays (B0, B1, B2). One upper tray and one lower tray are combined together
for use.

Product Description
Page 5 of 7
Figure 1 Construction of tray
Each tray is injection molded thermoplastic (Polypropylene) frame, over molded with
thermoforming resin (EVA). The support with protrusion (A) is for maxillary arch,
and the support with protrusion (B) is for mandibular arch.
9. Characteristic of device
(1) Principle of mandibular advancement
Two protrusions are designed on the lateral side of upper tray assembly and lower tray
assembly separately so as to fix the upper tray assembly and lower tray assembly
together.
By restricting the lower protrusion to be located in front of the upper protrusion, the
lower tray assembly is thereby restricted to the front side of the upper tray assembly,
ensuring that the lower dental arch remains in a forward position relative to the upper
dental arch during use.
(2) Realization of different mandibular advancement distance
By positioning the upper protrusion and the lower protrusion at different locations
within the upper tray assembly and the lower tray assembly, respectively, different
forward displacement distances of the lower tray assembly relative to the upper tray
assembly can be restricted (for example, the B2 protrusion is positioned further
rearward relative to the B0 protrusion, resulting in a greater forward displacement of
the mandible when assembled with the upper tray). Therefore, multiple combinations
of protrusions at different positions in the tray assemblies (i.e., multiple sets of
devices) can achieve restrictions on different forward displacement distances of the
lower dental arch.
There are 7 combinations for upper tray and lower tray, each combination has its
different mandibular advancement distance (0-6 mm). By selecting suitable upper and
lower trays and using the “Boil-and-Bite” method, users can customize the fit to their
dentition.

INTENDEDUSE
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance
the user 's lower jaw and maintain this position during
use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep.
It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
Usage Period: 6-12 months
Storage Period: 2 years

Operating and Storage Conditions:
Operating Temperature: +5°C to +40°C
Operating Humidity: Relative humidity 10% to 90%
Storage Temperature: -20°C to +45°C
Storage Humidity: Relative humidity 10% to 90%
Before first use, please read and follow the instruction
manual thoroughly, as proper use is crucial for the
effectiveness of the device.
2

WORKING PRINCIPLE
Normal Breathing:
Adequate muscle tone in the
throat and tongue keeps the airway
open.
Snoring:
Muscle relaxation leads to
partial airway obstruction; faster
airflow through the narrowed
passage creates turbulence,
causing tissue vibration.
3

Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA):
Complete relaxation of the muscles
leads to total airway blockage,
preventing airflow and causing
temporary breathing cessation.
Using the Device:
By maintaining the lower jaw in a
forward position, the airway
remains open, allowing for normal
breathing.
4

ONTRAINDICATIONS
Do not use the device if any of the following conditions
apply:
1. Under 18 years of age, as it may affect the develop-
ment of teeth and jawbones in adolescents.
2. Diagnosed with Central Sleep Apnea (CSA), which
differs from OSA.
3. Suffering from severe respiratory diseases, such as
asthma, severe OsA, or emphysema.
4. Experiencing periodontal disease, including loose
teeth, gum bleeding, oral ulcers, or cavities.
5

5. Having Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD)
or other temporomandibular joint issues.
6. Having had dental implants within the last 12
months.
7. Currently undergoing orthodontic treatment or
wearing braces, full dentures, or other dental applianc-
es.
8. Having severe misalignment or bite issues (jaw or
tooth pain when clenching).
6

WARNINGS
1. Use of the device may lead to:
· Tooth movement or changes in bite
· Gum or tooth soreness
· Joint discomfort
· Irritation inside the mouth
· Excessive drooling
· Obstructed mouth breathing
· Dry mouth
2. If severe adverse reactions, allergies, breathing
difficulties, or other respiratory conditions occur,
discontinue use of the device and consult a doctor
immediately.
3. The device is not suitable for treating OSA.

NITIALREMINDERS
1. The effectiveness of the device varies from person to
person. Some may notice a significant reduction in
snoring within a few days, while others may need several
weeks. Both scenarios are normal.
2. The device may restrict mouth breathing. If nasal
congestion occurs during sleep, it is advised to temporari-
ly discontinue use of the device or use medication to clear
the nasal passages.
3. The device is thoughtfully designed to balance both
comfort and functionality. Even when the user sleeps with
8

their mouth open, the device ensures a secure and stable
fit, minimizing the risk of sleep interruptions. Its ergo-
nomic design allows for natural swallowing and main-
tains stability and comfort throughout the night, providing
users with a safe and convenient wearing experience.
4. If discomfort or dislodgment wakes you during sleep,
remove the device and continue sleeping.
5. It takes time to adapt to a Lo8 Anti Snoring Mouth-
device to dislodge initially. Please continue using it.

Morning Reset Training
gGuide
Due to your jaw being accustomed to being extended
forward overnight, it is normal for your jaw to remain in a
forward position upon waking. This condition typically
reverts to normal occlusion within one to two hours after
removing the device.
Below are some simple exercises that can help alleviate
discomfort or reset the position of your jaw:
· Before starting the exercises, apply a warm, moist
compress to any sore areas on both sides of the jaw for
10 minutes.
· Place your index and middle fingers on the sides of
your jaw, you can find the correct spot by clenching

your jaw slightly.
· Relax the jaw muscles and gently massage in circular
motions. Be careful not to massage for more than 10
minutes.
· Consider taking a night off to allow your jaw muscles
to rest fully.
· Do not wear the device again until your jaw has
returned to its normal position.
· If symptoms persist for a long period or pain intensi-
fies, stop using the device and consult your doctor.

1. Purpose
This durability verification is to confirm that the device still can work well after
undergoing molding, normal use, and cleaning processes at least 365 times/cycles.
2. Scope of test
This test is applicable to the Anti Snoring Mouthpiece of RAM.SHAW PTE.LTD.
3. Device description
Product name: Anti Snoring Mouthpiece
Model: L08-BP, L08-PT, L08-BT, L08-TP, L08-TB, L08-PB
Size: Large (L) and Standard (S)
Intended use: Advance the user’s lower jaw and maintain this position during use,
opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep.
Usage period: 6-12 months
4. Test sample and sample size
Test sample: L08-BP with Large size.
For the difference between different models, they are only different in the color of
tray.
For the difference between different size, they are only different in the dimension of
tray.
Given that this test is mainly related to the characteristic of material - EVA, and
different models or different sizes use the same EVA, thus the L08-BP with large size
can represent all the models and size.
Type of test: Comparison test.
Sample size: 2 L08-BP are selected in this test, which make 2 Tray A0, 2 Tray A2, 2
Tray A4, 2 Tray B0, 2 Tray B1, 2 Tray B2.
1 Tray A0, 1 Tray A2, 1 Tray A4, 1 Tray B0, 1 Tray B1, 1 Tray B2, a total of 6
samples are selected as positive group, and another 6 samples (1 Tray A0, 1 Tray A2,
1 Tray A4, 1 Tray B0, 1 Tray B1, 1 Tray B2) are selected as blank group.
5. Acceptance criteria
Pre-test criteria:
Odour: No pungent odor, no odor.

4
Post-test criteria:
Odour: No pungent odor, no odor.
Shape of tray: Put the device on the denture, device can fit well with the denture.
(Note: Blank group is not require to evaluate shape of tray)
During the testing, other abnormal condition should also be documented.
6. Procedure
a. Prepare 2 L08-BP of one batch, and separate them into two groups: test group and
blank group.
b. Verify if all these samples meet the pre-test acceptance criteria and record the
results.
c. For blank group, they will be put into package box again until the end of
durability test. For test group, they will undergo one molding procedure and 365
times simulated use, and 365 times cleaning processes.
d. According to the instruction of user manual, prepare a pot with boiling water. And
then use a tweezer to submerge the samples in hot water above 80℃ for 1.5 to 2
minutes.
e. Use tweezer to remove the samples from the hot water. Use denture for molding
the specific shape. Then rinse with water until it is cooled.
f. Simulated occlusion. Wipe the dental model with the artificial saliva. Fix the
device on the dental model and simulate the position and direction of the teeth
during the occlusion process. Make sure that the teeth are completely closed.
Repeat the occlusions process for 10 times.
g. Squeeze dish soap on the device and then use soft brush to lightly brush the
device for 15 seconds to remove dirt.
h. Rinse with water at 25~30 degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.
i. Soak one dental appliance cleanser in 200ml of 30-35℃ water. Once bubble is
observed, put the device under solution for at least 5 minutes.
j. Take out the device and rinse the device with 20-25℃ water for 20 seconds .
k. Use dish towel to wipe dry the device.
l. Repeat f to k for 365 times.
m. For the first 180 times, verify if all these samples meet the post-test acceptance
criteria and record the results every 30 times.
n. For the last 185 times, verify if all these samples meet the post-test acceptance
criteria and record the results every 15 times.
o. Verify if all these samples meet the post-test acceptance criteria and record the
results the after 365 times.

SUMMARY 
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the extract of a test article for cytotoxicity to 
mammalian cells in culture by a method compliant with the requirements specified in ISO 
10993-5:2009. 
The test article was extracted with 5% FBS complete MEM  medium in sterile vessels for 
72(±2) hours at 37℃ ±1℃ incubator with a ratio of 3 cm2/mL.  T he negative control article 
and positive control article were extracted with ratios of 3 cm2/mL and 6 cm2/mL respectively 
at the same conditions.  The vehicle control was extracted at the same conditions of test article. 
At the end of the extraction period, the maintenance culture medi um were removed from test 
culture wells and 2 mL extracts were added in triplicates.  Then the plates were incubated for 
about 72 hours in 37℃±1℃ carbon dioxide incubator with high humidity and CO2% set as 5%.  
The cultures were evaluated for cytotoxic effects by microscopic examination at time points of 
24 hours, 48 hours and 72 hours.  The cytotoxic response of all extracts was evaluated.  
The results showed that vehicle control and negative control  retained a healthy normal 
appearance throughout the duration of the test and displayed no cytotoxic reaction, scored “0”, 
and met the validat ion acceptance criteria.  Positive control displayed severe cytotoxic 
reaction, scored “4”, and met the acceptance criteria. 
Test article extract, displayed no reactivity with the same scores of “ 0”, at time points of 
24 hours, 48 hours, and 72 hours. 
Base on the above results, this MEM elution assay was considered valid and it was concluded 
that the test article was NON-CYTOTOXIC under the conditions of this study.

5.1 Cell Line

in a 37℃±1℃ carbon dioxide incubator with high humidity and CO2% set as 5% .

supplemented with  10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).  The medium was also 
supplemented with the following: 2 mM L-glutamine, 100 units/mL penicillin, and 
100 µg/mL streptomycin.  The use of antibiotics in culture medium has not shown 
adverse effects when used for this assay.

The MEM elution assay is one of several in vitro mammalian cell tests which have 
been used to screen materials for their potential cytotoxicity.  The L -929 cell line 
has a history of use in assays of this type  and is recom mended in regulatory 
guidelines.

9 ASSAY EVALUATION 
(1) At the time points of 24, 48, and 72 hours, the plates were taken out and examined 
under 100× magnification microscope for signs of cytopathic effect.  Criteria for 
evaluating cytotoxicity included morphologic changes in cells, such as 
granulation, crenation, or rounding, and loss of viable cells from the monolayer 
by lysis or detachment. 
(2) A numerical score was assigned to each well using the following scale: 
Grade Reactivity Conditions of all Cultures 
0 None Discrete intracytoplasmic granules, no cell lysis, no reduction of cell growth 
1 Slight 
Not more than 20% of the cells are round, loosely attached, and 
without intracytoplasmic granules, or show changes in morphology; 
occasional lysed cells are present; only slight growth inhibition 
observable. 
2 Mild 
Not more than 50% of the cells are round, devoid of 
intracytoplasmic granules, no extensive cell lysis; not more than 
50% growth inhibition observable. 
3 Moderate 
Not more than 70% of the cell layers contain rounded cells or are 
lysed; cell layers not completely destroyed, but more than 50% 
growth inhibition observable. 
4 Severe Nearly complete or complete destruction of the cell layers. 
10 ASSAY VALIDITY 
Final evaluation of the validity of the assay and results were based upon the criteria 
listed below and scientific judgment. 
♦ The vehicle control s must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout the 
duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
♦ The negative controls must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout the 
duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
♦ Positive control must display a moderate to severe cytotoxic reaction, displaying 
a score of ‘3’ or ‘4’ by final reading of the test. 
11 TEST ARTICLE EVALUATION CRITERIA 
Negative Response: 
Sample cultures scores of “0”, “1”, or, “2” on all scoring points, the sample is considered 
to be “NONTOXIC” and will be reported as “NON- CYTOTOXIC”. 
Positive Response: 
Sample cultures scores “3” on some or all scoring points, the sample is considered to be 
“MODERATELY TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”. 
Sample cultures displaying scores “4” at any of the scoring points, the sample is 
considered “TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”.

11 TEST SYSTEM 
11.1 Cell Line 
The L -929 cells (ATCC cell line CCL -1) employed in this assay are mouse 
fibroblasts, and sub-cultured in this laboratory.  Cell lines which are mycoplasma -
free are purchased from the vendor and are kept frozen in the lab until use. 
To maintain the sensitivity, they are only sub -cultured for up to 15 passages and 
then discarded.  If a stock culture of a cell line is stored, storage shall be  in liquid 
nitrogen (about -196℃).  If the cells are grown from cultures taken from storage, 
remove the cryoprotectant, if present.  Subculture the cells at least once before use. 
11.2 Medium and Cell Culture Condition 
L-929 cells are grown and used as monolayers in disposable tissue culture  labware 
in a 37 ℃ incubator with high humidity and CO 2% set as 5%  at WuXi AppTec.   
The incubator temperature range will be 37℃±1℃, any conditions exceeds the 
range and lasts longer than one hour will be recorded as a deviation.  The medium 
used for growth of cells is minimal essential medium (MEM) supplemented with 
5% (v/v) fetal bovine serum (FBS).  The medium is also supplemented with the 
following:  2 mM L -glutamine, 100 units/mL penicillin, and 100 µ g/mL 
streptomycin.  WuXi AppTec has a long-standing history using antibiotics in 
culture medium.  The use of antibiotics in culture media has not shown adverse 
effects when used for this assay.  This is exhibited in the varying degrees of 
toxicity seen in the assay controls 
11.3 Justification for Selection of Test System 
The MEM elution assay is one of several in vitro mammalian cell tests, which  
have been used to screen materials for their potential cytotoxicity.  The L-929 cell 
line has a history of use in assays of this type. 
12 PROCEDURES 
(BIO-047 and BIO-049) 
 L-929 cells will be plated at a sufficient seeding density for about 3 days before 
use.  Prior to dosing, the cell cultures will be examined to ensure they have 
formed a subconfluent monolayer (approximately 80% confluency) and that they 
appear uniform and viable.  
 2 mL aliquots of the test article and control article extracts will be plated in 
triplicate onto the cell line. 
 The cell cultures will be incubated in a humidified atmosphere for appropriately 
72 hours.  The monolayers will be evaluated for cytotoxi c effects at time points 
of 24, 48, and 72 hours .  At each incubation period the cell cultures will be 
observed for signs of cytopathic effect (CPE) including lysis, crenation, plaques, 
and excessive rounding of cells.

13 CYTOTOXICITY SCORING 
Criteria for evaluating cytotoxicity will include morphologic changes in cells, such as 
granulation, crenation, or rounding, and loss of viable cells from the monolayer by 
lysis or detachment.   The validity of the test requires that neg ative control cultures 
maintain a healthy normal appearance throughout the duration of the test.  Degrees of 
toxicity are scored as follows. 
Grade Reactivity Conditions of all Cultures 
0 None Discrete intracytoplasmic granules; no cell lysis, no reduction of cell growth. 
1 Slight 
Not more than 20% of the cells are round, loosely attached, and without 
intracytoplasmic granules, or show changes in morphology; occasional 
lysed cells are present; only slight growth inhibition observable. 
2 Mild 
Not more than 50% of the cells are round, devoid of intracytoplasmic 
granules, no extensive cell lysis; not more than 50% growth inhibition 
observable. 
3 Moderate 
Not more than 70% of the cell layers contain rounded cells or are lysed; 
cells layers not completely destroyed, but more than 50% growth 
inhibition observable. 
4 Severe Nearly complete or complete destruction of the cell layers. 
14 RESULTS ANALYSIS 
14.1 Assay Validity 
Final evaluation of the validity of the assay and test article results will be based 
upon the criteria listed below and scientific judgment. 
 The vehicle controls must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout the 
duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
 The negative controls must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout 
the duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
 Positive control must display a moderate to severe cytotoxic reaction, 
displaying a score of ‘3’ or ‘4’ by final reading of the test. 
14.2 Test Article Evaluation Criteria 
Negative Response: 
Sample cultures scores of “0”, “1”, or, “2” on all scoring points, the sampl e is 
considered to be “NONTOXIC” and will be reported as “NON- CYTOTOXIC”. 
Positive Response: 
Sample cultures scores “3” on some or all scoring points, the sample is considered 
to be “MODERATELY TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”. 
Sample cultures d isplaying scores “4” at any of the scoring points, the sample is 
considered “TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”.

SUMMARY 
The test article, Anti Snoring Mouthpiece, Lot No. HSMYK002250221, was evaluated for the 
potential sensitization capacity in a guinea pig maximization sensitization test.  The study was 
conducted in accordance with the guidelines ISO 10993-10. 
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was sampled and extracted with the ratio of 3 cm2/mL 
at (50±2) ℃ for (72±2) hours.  The extraction vehicles were saline and sesame oil. 
A total of 34 femal e guinea pigs, approximately 4 to 6 weeks old and weighing 366.05 to 
457.86 g at initiation of dosing, were arbitrarily assigned to 4 groups (Negative control:  6/group; 
Test:  11/group). 
All animals were intradermally  and topically inducted, and then received a challenge patch  
(Except for animal No.4510).  Each challenge site w as scored at approximately 24±2 h and 
48±2 h following challenge.  The observation was conducted daily during the in-life phase on 
all animals.   The body weight was collected prior to the first dosing and on the day of 
termination for all animals. 
The dermal reactions following challenge showed: 
The positive sensitization rate to all control animals was 0%. 
The positive sensitization rate to all test animals was 0%. 
There was no test article related abnormality in clinical observation, and no animal with the 
body weight and body weight change were abnormal throughout the study. 
Under the conditions of this study, the saline and sesame oil extracts of test article did not show 
evidence of causing sensitization response in the guinea pigs.  Therefore, it is concluded that 
the test article has no potential for skin sensitization.

13 EVALUATION CRITERION 
After challenge or re -challenge dosing, grades of ‘1’ or greater in the test groups 
generally indicate sensitization, provided grades of less than ‘1’ are observed in the 
control animals.  If grades of ‘1’ or greater are noted in control animals, then the 
reactions of the test animals which exceed the most severe control reaction are presumed 
to be due to sensitization.  If the response is equivocal, re-challenge is recommended to 
confirm the results from the first challenge.  The outcome of the test is presented as the 
frequency of positive challenge results in test and control animals. 
Occasionally, the test group has a greater number of animals showing a response than 
the controls, although the intensity of the reaction is not greater than that observed on 
the controls.  In these instances, a re-challenge may be necessary to define the response 
clearly.  A re-challenge shall be carried out 1 to 2 weeks after the first challenge using 
the same animals. 
Note:  Background or artifactual reactions from fur clipping, patch edge, or nonspecific 
FCA effects were not considered as evidence of sensitization.

(Reference SOP: BIO-004) 
At least 34 guinea pigs of the same sex, will be used for this test and will be arbitrarily 
assigned to 4 groups (≥6 animals/control group, ≥11 animals/ test group).  All animals 
will be intradermally and topically inducted, and then received a challenge patch.  Score 
each challenge site approximately 24 h and 48 h following challenge. 
The observation will be conducted daily during the in-life phase.  The body weight will 
be collected at least once prior to the first dosing and once on the day of termination for 
all animals.

8.1 Dosing Procedures 
8.1.1 Induction I/Intradermal Induction Phase 
The dorsum will be prepared by removing the fur with an electric clipper prior 
to all steps in the test procedure. 
The first day of intraderma l induction dosing will be designated as Day 1.  
Formulations will be prepared for the control or test groups animals as indicated 
in  Table 8-1 and Figure 8-2.  The prepared formulations will be injected in 
pairs on each side of the dorsal midline.  Injections ‘a’ and ‘b’ will be given in 
close proximity to each othe r cranially; injection ‘c’ will be located caudally.   
Each injection site will be intradermally injected 0.1 mL. 
8.1.2 Induction II/Topical Induction Phase 
Approximately 24 ± 2 hours before topical induction administration, all the 
injection sites skin will be pai nted with about 0.5  mL/animal of 10%  sodium 
lauryl sulfate (SLS) in liquid paraffin.  If necessary, re-clip the dorsal test sites 
on all the test and control animals with a clipper, as necessary to expose the 
skin before SLS application.  Clean with diluted alcohol before SLS application.

positive test completion date. Positive control results will be presented in the final 
report.  
17 EVALUTION CRITERIA 
After challenge or re -challenge dosing, grades of ‘1’ or greater in the test groups 
generally indicate sensitization, provided grades of less than ‘1’ are observed in the 
control animals.  If grades of ‘1’ or greater are noted in control animals, then the 
reactions of the test animals which exceed the most severe control reaction are presumed 
to be due to sensitization.  If the response is equivocal, re-challenge is recommended to 
confirm the results from the first challenge.  The outcome of the test is presented as the 
frequency of positive challenge results in test and control animals.

SUMMARY 
The test article is Anti Snoring Mouthpiece , Batch/Lot No. HSMYK002250221.  
Intracutaneous reactivity test in rabbits was carried out according to standards ISO 10993-23. 
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was sampled and extracted with the ratio of 3 cm2/mL 
at 50±2℃ for 72±2 hours.  The extraction vehicles were saline and sesame oil. 
A total of 3  New Zealand White rabbits of age approximately 4~5 months and body weights 
ranged from 3.08 to 3.14 kg administered with 0.2 mL doses of each extract into five separate 
sites on the left side of the back of each rabbit.  Similarly, each control vehicle was injected on 
the right s ide of the back of each rabbit.   The injection sites were observed immediately 
post-injection (within 5 mins) and at 24, 48, and 72 hours post injection and were scored at 24, 
48, and 72 hour time points.  The clinical symptoms except skin reactions were observed at 
each time point post injection. 
The final test article score is 0 (Saline) and 0 ( Sesame oil).  No abnormal clinical symptoms 
except skin reactions were observed at all time points. 
Under the conditions of this study, the difference between the test extracts and their respective 
control mean scores were less than 1.0.  The test article met the requirement of the test, did not 
cause local dermal irritant effects.

4 EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN 
3 healthy adult male New Zealand white rabbits were used in this study.  The test article 
extracts and vehicle controls were injected intracutan eously on both sides of the back 
of the animals in pairs on the day of administration.  
The injection sites were observed immediately post injection (within 5 mins) and at 24, 
48 and 72 hours post injection and were scored at 24, 48, and 72 hour time points.  The 
clinical symptoms  other than skin reactions were observed at each time point post 
injection. 
4.1 Dose Administration 
The fur on the backs of animals were closely clipped within a 4 to 18 -hour period 
before treatment to allow a sufficient area on both sides of the spine for injection of 
the extracts and controls.   
The day of dosing was designated as Day 1.  At five sites on the left side of the 
spinal column on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the saline (polar) or sesame oil (non-polar) 
extracts were injected.  Similarly, at five sites on the right side of the spinal column 
on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the concurrent vehicle controls were injected.  The 
arrangement of the injection sites is presented as follows, not less than 1cm intervals 
between 2 sites.  Prior to administration, agitate d each extract prior to withdrawal 
of injection doses to ensure even distribution of the extracted matter. 
 
4.2 Dose Level Selection and Justification 
Undiluted extracts and controls were administered, the dosage volume is 0.2 mL/site, 
as recommended by standard ISO 10993-23. 
4.3 Route of Administration and Justification 
Intracutaneous injection is the recommende d dosing route of  standard ISO 10993-
23.

12 EVALUATION CRITERION 
All erythema grades plus edema grades at 24±2, 48±2 and 72±2 hours are totalled 
separately for each test extract or control for each individual animal.  To calculate the 
score of a test extract or control on each individual animal, each of the totals is divided 
by 15 (3 scoring time points × 5 test or control sample injection sites).   To determine 
the overall mean score for each test extract and each corresponding control, the scores 
were added for the three animals and divided by three.  The final test article score is 
obtained by subtracting the score of the control from the test article score.

3 healthy adult New Zealand white rabbits of the same sex will be used in this study.  
The test article extracts and vehicle controls will be injected intracutaneously on both 
sides of the back of the animals in pairs on the day of administration. 
The appearance of each site will be observed immediately post injection and at 24, 
48 and 72 hours post injection.  The skin reactions at the 24, 48 , and 72  hour time 
interval will be graded  and any clinical symptoms other than  skin reactions will be 
observed at each time point post injection. 
8.1 Dose Administration 
The fur on the backs of animals will be closely clipped within a 4 to 18-hour period 
before treatment to allow a sufficient area on both sides of the spine for injection of 
the extracts and controls.  Mechanical irritation and trauma to the skin will be 
avoided during clipping. 
The day of dosing will be designated as Day 1.   At five sites on the left side of the 
spinal column on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the saline (polar) or sesame oil (non-polar) 
extract will be injected.  Similarly, at five sites on the right side of the spinal column 
on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the concurrent vehicle controls will be injected.  The 
arrangement of the injection sites is presented as follows, not less than 1cm intervals 
between 2 sites.  Prior to administration, agitate each extract prior to withdrawal of 
injection doses to ensure even distribution of the extracted matter. 
 
8.2 Dose Level Selection and Justification 
Undiluted controls and test article extracts will be administered, the dosage volume 
is 0.2 mL/site, as recommended by standard ISO 10993-23. 
8.3 Route of Administration and Justification 
Intracutaneous injection is the recommended dosing route of standard ISO 10993-
23.

separately for each test extract or control for each individual animal.  To calculate the 
score of a test extract or control on each individual animal, each of the totals is divided 
by 15 (3  scoring time points × 5 test or control sample injection sites).  To determine

Indications for use
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance the user's lower jaw and
maintain this position during use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep.
It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
Device Description
The L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is an intraoral device that is used to maintain
the lower jaw in a forward position to increase pharyngeal space so as to improve the
ability to exchange air and decrease air turbulence, a causative factor in snoring.
L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece includes three upper trays (A0, A2, A4) and three
lower trays (B0, B1, B2). One upper tray and one lower tray are combined together
for use. By randomly combining one upper tray with one lower tray, the device can be
used for advancing lower jaw from 0mm to 6mm.
Considering that the size of the oral cavity varies among different groups of people,
L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to be available for two size (L and S).
Even though the dimensions of these sizes of Anti Snoring Mouthpiece are different,
by positioning the upper protrusion and the lower protrusion at different locations
within the upper tray assembly and the lower tray assembly respectively, advancement
distance of 0-6 mm can still be realized.

According to Use of International Standard ISO 10993-1, "Biological evaluation of

for additional testing.
Taking into consideration of FDA guidance “Intraoral Devices for Snoring and/or
Obstructive Sleep Apnea - Class II Special Controls Guidance Document for Industry
and FDA”, ISO-10993 -5, -10, which include cytotoxicity, sensitization, Irritation,
should be considered.

3.2. Details of Testing
3.2.1. Cytotoxicity(Test Report No.: W25-0003-BAR)
The test was performed in accordance with ISO 10993-5:2009.

7 / 8
The test article was extracted using 5% FBS complete MEM medium at 3 cm²/mL for
72±2 hours at 37±1°C. The negative and positive controls were extracted at 3 cm²/mL
and 6 cm²/mL, respectively, under the same conditions, and the vehicle control was
extracted identically to the test article.
After extraction, 2 mL of each extract were added in triplicate to culture wells and
incubated for about 72 hours at 37±1°C with 5% CO₂ and high humidity.
Cultures were examined microscopically for cytotoxicity at 24, 48, and 72 hours. The
vehicle and negative controls showed no cytotoxicity (score “0”), meeting acceptance
criteria. The positive control showed severe cytotoxicity (score “4”), also meeting
criteria.
The test article extract showed no reactivity (score “0”) at all time points.
Base on the above results, this MEM elution assay was considered valid and it was
concluded that the test article was NON-CYTOTOXIC under the conditions of this
study.
3.2.2. Sensitization(Test Report No.: W25-0002-BVO )
The test was performed in accordance with ISO 10993-10:2021.
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was sampled and extracted with the ratio of 3
cm2 /mL at (50±2) ℃ for (72±2) hours. The extraction vehicles were saline and
sesame oil.
A total of 34 female guinea pigs, approximately 4 to 6 weeks old and weighing
366.05 to 457.86 g at initiation of dosing, were arbitrarily assigned to 4 groups
(Negative control: 6/group; Test: 11/group)
All animals were intradermally and topically inducted, and then received a challenge
patch (Except for animal No.4510). Each challenge site was scored at approximately
24±2 h and 48±2 h following challenge.
Under the conditions of this study, the saline and sesame oil extracts of test article did
not show evidence of causing sensitization response in the guinea pigs. Therefore, it is
concluded that the test article has no potential for skin sensitization.
3.2.3. Irritation or Intracutaneous reactivity(Test Report No.: W25-0001-BVO )
The test was performed in accordance with ISO 10993-23:2021.
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was extracted at 3 cm²/mL in saline and
sesame oil at 50±2°C for 72±2 hours.
Three New Zealand White rabbits (aged 4-5 months, weight 3.08-3.14 kg) received
0.2 mL injections of each extract at five sites on the left back. The control vehicles
were similarly injected on the right back.
Injection sites were observed immediately and at 24, 48, and 72 hours, with scores

8 / 8
recorded at the latter three time points. Clinical symptoms (other than skin reactions)
were also monitored.
The final test article scores were 0 for both saline and sesame oil extracts. No
abnormal clinical symptoms, other than skin reactions, were observed at any time
point.
Under the conditions of this study, the difference between the test extracts and their
respective control mean scores were less than 1.0. The test article met the requirement
of the test, did not cause local dermal irritant effects.
4. Conclusion
According to the results, we consider that the device under evaluation has acceptable
bio-compatibility.

Indication for use/Intended Use
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance the user's lower jaw and maintain this position during use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep. It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
Contraindications
Do not use the device if any of the following conditions apply: 
1.Under 18 years of age, as it may affect the development of teeth and jawbones in adolescents.
2.Diagnosed with Central Sleep Apnea (CSA), which differs from OSA.
3.Suffering from severe respiratory diseases, such as asthma, severe OSA, or emphysema.
4.Experiencing periodontal disease, including loose teeth, gum bleeding, oral ulcers, or cavities.
5.Having Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD) or other temporomandibular joint issues.
6.Having had dental implants within the last 12 months.
7.Currently undergoing orthodontic treatment or wearing braces, full dentures, or other dental appliances.
8.Having severe misalignment or bite issues (jaw or tooth pain when clenching).
Warnings
1. Use of the device may lead to:
1) Tooth movement or changes in bite
2) Gum or tooth soreness
3) Joint discomfort
4) Irritation inside the mouth
5) Excessive drooling
6) Obstructed mouth breathing
7) Dry mouth
2. If severe adverse reactions, allergies, breathing difficulties, or other respiratory conditions occur, discontinue use of the device and consult a doctor immediately.
3. The device is not suitable for treating OSA.
Principles
Normal Breathing:
For normal person, adequate muscle tone in the throat and tongue keeps the airway open.
Snoring
For snoring patients, they have muscle relaxation leading to partial airway obstruction. Faster airflow through the narrow passage creates turbulence, causing tissue vibration.
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)
Complete relaxation of the muscles leads to total airway blockage, preventing airflow and causing temporary breathing cessation.
By using the device, it can maintain the lower jaw in a forward position to increase pharyngeal space so as to keep the airway open. Thus allowing for normal breathing.
Construction 
L08 series Anti Snoring Mouthpiece includes three upper trays (A0, A2, A4) and three lower trays (B0, B1, B2). One upper tray and one lower tray are combined together for use.
The constructions of tray are shown below:
Upper tray

Figure 1 Construction of tray
Each tray is injection molded thermoplastic (Polypropylene) frame, over molded with thermoforming resin (EVA). The support with protrusion (A) is for maxillary arch, and the support with protrusion (B) is for mandibular arch. 
Characteristic of device
Principle of mandibular advancement
Two protrusions are designed on the lateral side of upper tray assembly and lower tray assembly separately so as to fix the upper tray assembly and lower tray assembly together.
By restricting the lower protrusion to be located in front of the upper protrusion, the lower tray assembly is thereby restricted to the front side of the upper tray assembly, ensuring that the lower dental arch remains in a forward position relative to the upper dental arch during use. 
Realization of different mandibular advancement distance
By positioning the upper protrusion and the lower protrusion at different locations within the upper tray assembly and the lower tray assembly, respectively, different forward displacement distances of the lower tray assembly relative to the upper tray assembly can be restricted (for example, the B2 protrusion is positioned further rearward relative to the B0 protrusion, resulting in a greater forward displacement of the mandible when assembled with the upper tray). Therefore, multiple combinations of protrusions at different positions in the tray assemblies (i.e., multiple sets of devices) can achieve restrictions on different forward displacement distances of the lower dental arch.
There are 7 combinations for upper tray and lower tray, each combination has its different mandibular advancement distance (0-6 mm). By selecting suitable upper and lower trays and using the “Boil-and-Bite” method, users can customize the fit to their dentition.

Table 3 Accelerated ageing equipment
Accelerated ageing model
The accelerated ageing model is referenced to ASTM F 1980-21-Standard Guide for Accelerated ageing of Sterile Barrier Systems for Medical Devices.
It is based on the assumption that the chemical reactions involved in material degradation follow the Arrhenius reaction rate function. The equation is shown below:
AAF = Q10{(TAA-TRT)/10} (1)
Where
AAF: Accelerated ageing factor
Q10: ageing factor for a 10°C increase or decrease in temperature
TAA: Accelerated ageing Temperature
TRT: Temperature under normal storage conditions
Then the accelerated ageing time (AAT) can be calculated by the following equation:
AAT = Desired (RT)/AAF (2)
Where
AAT: Accelerated ageing Time
RT: Real-time ageing Time
Accelerated ageing time calculation
Typically, the storage temperature is between 20 to 25℃. Therefore, a temperature of 25℃ is considered a normal storage temperature. Taken into account the material characteristic of device under test, accelerated ageing temperature is selected as 60℃ and Q10 is selected as 2.
Based on the above formula, the accelerated ageing time is calculated as follows:
Therefore, the accelerated ageing time for this validation is approximately 65 days.
Acceptance criteria
Pre-ageing criteria:
Visual check: No cracks, no scratches, no deformation.
Odour: No pungent odor, no odor.
Post-ageing criteria:
Visual check: No cracks, no scratches, no deformation.
Odour: No pungent odor, no odor.
Molding: Verify if the device still can be molded by using denture.
Other abnormal condition should also be documented.
Test procedure
Prepare 10 L08-BP of one batch, and ensure that all of the samples can meet pre-test acceptance criteria and record the result.
Put all these samples into accelerated ageing equipment, and the temperature and humidity of accelerated ageing equipment is set to:

Once the accelerated time is reached, take out the samples, and check if these samples meet the post-test acceptance criteria and record the results.

INTENDEDUSE
The Anti Snoring Mouthpiece is designed to advance
the user 's lower jaw and maintain this position during
use, opening the airway to reduce snoring during sleep.
It is intended for adults with at least 18 years old.
Usage Period: 6-12 months
Storage Period: 2 years

Operating and Storage Conditions:
Operating Temperature: +5°C to +40°C
Operating Humidity: Relative humidity 10% to 90%
Storage Temperature: -20°C to +45°C
Storage Humidity: Relative humidity 10% to 90%
Before first use, please read and follow the instruction
manual thoroughly, as proper use is crucial for the
effectiveness of the device.
2

WORKING PRINCIPLE
Normal Breathing:
Adequate muscle tone in the
throat and tongue keeps the airway
open.
Snoring:
Muscle relaxation leads to
partial airway obstruction; faster
airflow through the narrowed
passage creates turbulence,
causing tissue vibration.
3

Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA):
Complete relaxation of the muscles
leads to total airway blockage,
preventing airflow and causing
temporary breathing cessation.
Using the Device:
By maintaining the lower jaw in a
forward position, the airway
remains open, allowing for normal
breathing.
4

ONTRAINDICATIONS
Do not use the device if any of the following conditions
apply:
1. Under 18 years of age, as it may affect the develop-
ment of teeth and jawbones in adolescents.
2. Diagnosed with Central Sleep Apnea (CSA), which
differs from OSA.
3. Suffering from severe respiratory diseases, such as
asthma, severe OsA, or emphysema.
4. Experiencing periodontal disease, including loose
teeth, gum bleeding, oral ulcers, or cavities.
5

5. Having Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD)
or other temporomandibular joint issues.
6. Having had dental implants within the last 12
months.
7. Currently undergoing orthodontic treatment or
wearing braces, full dentures, or other dental applianc-
es.
8. Having severe misalignment or bite issues (jaw or
tooth pain when clenching).
6

WARNINGS
1. Use of the device may lead to:
· Tooth movement or changes in bite
· Gum or tooth soreness
· Joint discomfort
· Irritation inside the mouth
· Excessive drooling
· Obstructed mouth breathing
· Dry mouth
2. If severe adverse reactions, allergies, breathing
difficulties, or other respiratory conditions occur,
discontinue use of the device and consult a doctor
immediately.
3. The device is not suitable for treating OSA.

NITIALREMINDERS
1. The effectiveness of the device varies from person to
person. Some may notice a significant reduction in
snoring within a few days, while others may need several
weeks. Both scenarios are normal.
2. The device may restrict mouth breathing. If nasal
congestion occurs during sleep, it is advised to temporari-
ly discontinue use of the device or use medication to clear
the nasal passages.
3. The device is thoughtfully designed to balance both
comfort and functionality. Even when the user sleeps with
8

their mouth open, the device ensures a secure and stable
fit, minimizing the risk of sleep interruptions. Its ergo-
nomic design allows for natural swallowing and main-
tains stability and comfort throughout the night, providing
users with a safe and convenient wearing experience.
4. If discomfort or dislodgment wakes you during sleep,
remove the device and continue sleeping.
5. It takes time to adapt to a Lo8 Anti Snoring Mouth-
device to dislodge initially. Please continue using it.

Morning Reset Training
gGuide
Due to your jaw being accustomed to being extended
forward overnight, it is normal for your jaw to remain in a
forward position upon waking. This condition typically
reverts to normal occlusion within one to two hours after
removing the device.
Below are some simple exercises that can help alleviate
discomfort or reset the position of your jaw:
· Before starting the exercises, apply a warm, moist
compress to any sore areas on both sides of the jaw for
10 minutes.
· Place your index and middle fingers on the sides of
your jaw, you can find the correct spot by clenching

your jaw slightly.
· Relax the jaw muscles and gently massage in circular
motions. Be careful not to massage for more than 10
minutes.
· Consider taking a night off to allow your jaw muscles
to rest fully.
· Do not wear the device again until your jaw has
returned to its normal position.
· If symptoms persist for a long period or pain intensi-
fies, stop using the device and consult your doctor.

3.2.5 Extraction
After cleaning the test group, First, rinse the test sample with the eluent, then wipe the test
sample with a gauze soaked in the eluent, and repeat the steps three times. Each time the
gauze is changed, then the wiped gauze is cut into small pieces and placed in 100mL of
elution solution, and ultrasonically oscillated for 5 minutes (40khz). Extract four times and
analyze each eluent. Determine the protein content and hemoglobin content.
The positive device control group was extracted 4 times according to the above method, and
the recovery efficiency was calculated.
Negative device control group: The test product is treated in the same manner as the test
group, but the test product is not contaminated.
Negative sample control group: Place sterile gauze that has not come into contact with the test
sample into the elution solution (100mL), shake for 5 minutes, and prepare 3 parallel samples.
Positive sample control group: The ATS was diluted with eluent, the protein concentration
was 2.5 μg/mL, shook well for 5 minutes, and 3 parallel samples were prepared. The ATS was
diluted with the extraction medium, the hemoglobin concentration was 0.5 μg/mL, and 3
parallel samples were prepared by shaking well for 5 minutes.

Attachment(Precautions & Pretreatment steps)
Note: Taking into account of the worst case of cleaning procedure, the 15 samples will be
preprocessed by molding and occlusion based on the following two reasons:
(1)User needs touse“Boil-and-Bite"method to customize the fit to their dentition before
using the device.
(2)The surface of samples will become rougher after molding and occlusion, which will
increase the difficulty of cleaning.
The preprocessing method is shown below:
1)Fill a pot with water enough to submerge the device.
2)Wait for the water to boil and then stop heating
3)Use a spoon or tweezers to submerge the device under hot water above 80°C (preferably
above 90°C)for 1.5 to 2 minutes.
4)Remove the device from the hot water using a spoon or tweezers, and shake off any excess
water.
5)Cool for 5 to 10 seconds.
6)Put the upper tray of the device in the dental model, and press down the dental model to
simulate occlusion.
7)Take out the upper tray with occlusal mark.
8)Then put another lower tray of the device in the dental model, and press down the dental
model.
9)Take out the device with occlusal mark.
10)Rinse the upper tray and lower tray with water of 20-30°C until it is cooled.
In order for consistency, 15 samples should be preprocessed by the same dental model.

SUMMARY 
The test article is Anti Snoring Mouthpiece , Batch/Lot No. HSMYK002250221.  
Intracutaneous reactivity test in rabbits was carried out according to standards ISO 10993-23. 
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was sampled and extracted with the ratio of 3 cm2/mL 
at 50±2℃ for 72±2 hours.  The extraction vehicles were saline and sesame oil. 
A total of 3  New Zealand White rabbits of age approximately 4~5 months and body weights 
ranged from 3.08 to 3.14 kg administered with 0.2 mL doses of each extract into five separate 
sites on the left side of the back of each rabbit.  Similarly, each control vehicle was injected on 
the right s ide of the back of each rabbit.   The injection sites were observed immediately 
post-injection (within 5 mins) and at 24, 48, and 72 hours post injection and were scored at 24, 
48, and 72 hour time points.  The clinical symptoms except skin reactions were observed at 
each time point post injection. 
The final test article score is 0 (Saline) and 0 ( Sesame oil).  No abnormal clinical symptoms 
except skin reactions were observed at all time points. 
Under the conditions of this study, the difference between the test extracts and their respective 
control mean scores were less than 1.0.  The test article met the requirement of the test, did not 
cause local dermal irritant effects.

4 EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN 
3 healthy adult male New Zealand white rabbits were used in this study.  The test article 
extracts and vehicle controls were injected intracutan eously on both sides of the back 
of the animals in pairs on the day of administration.  
The injection sites were observed immediately post injection (within 5 mins) and at 24, 
48 and 72 hours post injection and were scored at 24, 48, and 72 hour time points.  The 
clinical symptoms  other than skin reactions were observed at each time point post 
injection. 
4.1 Dose Administration 
The fur on the backs of animals were closely clipped within a 4 to 18 -hour period 
before treatment to allow a sufficient area on both sides of the spine for injection of 
the extracts and controls.   
The day of dosing was designated as Day 1.  At five sites on the left side of the 
spinal column on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the saline (polar) or sesame oil (non-polar) 
extracts were injected.  Similarly, at five sites on the right side of the spinal column 
on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the concurrent vehicle controls were injected.  The 
arrangement of the injection sites is presented as follows, not less than 1cm intervals 
between 2 sites.  Prior to administration, agitate d each extract prior to withdrawal 
of injection doses to ensure even distribution of the extracted matter. 
 
4.2 Dose Level Selection and Justification 
Undiluted extracts and controls were administered, the dosage volume is 0.2 mL/site, 
as recommended by standard ISO 10993-23. 
4.3 Route of Administration and Justification 
Intracutaneous injection is the recommende d dosing route of  standard ISO 10993-
23.

12 EVALUATION CRITERION 
All erythema grades plus edema grades at 24±2, 48±2 and 72±2 hours are totalled 
separately for each test extract or control for each individual animal.  To calculate the 
score of a test extract or control on each individual animal, each of the totals is divided 
by 15 (3 scoring time points × 5 test or control sample injection sites).   To determine 
the overall mean score for each test extract and each corresponding control, the scores 
were added for the three animals and divided by three.  The final test article score is 
obtained by subtracting the score of the control from the test article score.

3 healthy adult New Zealand white rabbits of the same sex will be used in this study.  
The test article extracts and vehicle controls will be injected intracutaneously on both 
sides of the back of the animals in pairs on the day of administration. 
The appearance of each site will be observed immediately post injection and at 24, 
48 and 72 hours post injection.  The skin reactions at the 24, 48 , and 72  hour time 
interval will be graded  and any clinical symptoms other than  skin reactions will be 
observed at each time point post injection. 
8.1 Dose Administration 
The fur on the backs of animals will be closely clipped within a 4 to 18-hour period 
before treatment to allow a sufficient area on both sides of the spine for injection of 
the extracts and controls.  Mechanical irritation and trauma to the skin will be 
avoided during clipping. 
The day of dosing will be designated as Day 1.   At five sites on the left side of the 
spinal column on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the saline (polar) or sesame oil (non-polar) 
extract will be injected.  Similarly, at five sites on the right side of the spinal column 
on each rabbit, 0.2 mL of the concurrent vehicle controls will be injected.  The 
arrangement of the injection sites is presented as follows, not less than 1cm intervals 
between 2 sites.  Prior to administration, agitate each extract prior to withdrawal of 
injection doses to ensure even distribution of the extracted matter. 
 
8.2 Dose Level Selection and Justification 
Undiluted controls and test article extracts will be administered, the dosage volume 
is 0.2 mL/site, as recommended by standard ISO 10993-23. 
8.3 Route of Administration and Justification 
Intracutaneous injection is the recommended dosing route of standard ISO 10993-
23.

15 ASSAY VALIDITY 
Final evaluation of the validity of the assay and test article results will be based upon 
the criteria listed below and scientific judgment. 
 Each of five sodium chloride control sites in each animal at all timepoints 
erythema or edema is Grade 0.  
 Each of five oil control sites in each animal at all timepoints  erythema or edema 
is ≤ Grade 1. 
 The test completion date is within 6 months of the most recent valid periodic 
positive test completion date.  Positive control results will be presented in the final 
report. 
16 EVALUATION CRITERION 
All erythema grades plus edema grades at 24± 2, 48± 2 and 72± 2 hours are totalled 
separately for each test extract or control for each individual animal.  To calculate the 
score of a test extract or control on each individual animal, each of the totals is divided 
by 15 (3  scoring time points × 5 test or control sample injection sites).  To determine 
the overall mean score for each test extract and each corresponding control, the scores 
will be added for the three animals and divided by three.  The final test article score is 
obtained by subtracting the score of the control from the test article score. 
The requirements of the test are met if the final test article score is 1.0 or less.

SUMMARY 
The test article, Anti Snoring Mouthpiece, Lot No. HSMYK002250221, was evaluated for the 
potential sensitization capacity in a guinea pig maximization sensitization test.  The study was 
conducted in accordance with the guidelines ISO 10993-10. 
Under aseptic conditions, the test article was sampled and extracted with the ratio of 3 cm2/mL 
at (50±2) ℃ for (72±2) hours.  The extraction vehicles were saline and sesame oil. 
A total of 34 femal e guinea pigs, approximately 4 to 6 weeks old and weighing 366.05 to 
457.86 g at initiation of dosing, were arbitrarily assigned to 4 groups (Negative control:  6/group; 
Test:  11/group). 
All animals were intradermally  and topically inducted, and then received a challenge patch  
(Except for animal No.4510).  Each challenge site w as scored at approximately 24±2 h and 
48±2 h following challenge.  The observation was conducted daily during the in-life phase on 
all animals.   The body weight was collected prior to the first dosing and on the day of 
termination for all animals. 
The dermal reactions following challenge showed: 
The positive sensitization rate to all control animals was 0%. 
The positive sensitization rate to all test animals was 0%. 
There was no test article related abnormality in clinical observation, and no animal with the 
body weight and body weight change were abnormal throughout the study. 
Under the conditions of this study, the saline and sesame oil extracts of test article did not show 
evidence of causing sensitization response in the guinea pigs.  Therefore, it is concluded that 
the test article has no potential for skin sensitization.

4.1 Dosing Procedures 
4.1.1 Induction I/Intradermal Induction Phase 
The dorsum was prepared by removing the fur with an electric clipper prior to 
all steps in the test procedure. 
The first day of intradermal induc tion dosing was designated as Day 1.  
Formulations were prepared for the contro l or test groups fo r each animal as 
indicated in Table 4-1 and Figure 4-2.  The prepared formulations were injected 
in pairs on each side of the dorsal midline.  Injections ‘a’ and ‘b’ were given in 
close proximity to each other cranially; injection ‘c’ was located caudally.  Each 
injection site was intradermally injected 0.1 mL. 
4.1.2 Induction II/Topical Induction Phase 
On Day 7, all the injection sites skin were painted with about 0.5 mL/animal of 
10% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in liqui d paraffin.  Dorsal test sites on all 
the test and control animals were clipped to expose the skin before SDS 
application.  Skin was cleaned with diluted alcohol before 10% SDS 
application.  Before topical induction, the remaining residue was gently wiped 
from the area with gauze. 
The topical induction administratio n was conducted as indicated in Table 4-1 
and Figure 4-2 on Day 8. 
Test Group(s):  An appropriately sized (approximately 2 cm × 4 cm) filter paper 
patch-soaked test article extract (About 0.3 mL), was applied to cover as much 
of the injection sites as possible.  The trunk of each animal was wrapped for 
approximately 48±2 hours with a secured with tape and expandable wrapping 
material.  
Control Group(s):  The animals were exposed to the control vehicle in the same 
manner as the test group. 
The patches were removed approxi mately 48±2 hours (Day 10) after 
application.

13 EVALUATION CRITERION 
After challenge or re -challenge dosing, grades of ‘1’ or greater in the test groups 
generally indicate sensitization, provided grades of less than ‘1’ are observed in the 
control animals.  If grades of ‘1’ or greater are noted in control animals, then the 
reactions of the test animals which exceed the most severe control reaction are presumed 
to be due to sensitization.  If the response is equivocal, re-challenge is recommended to 
confirm the results from the first challenge.  The outcome of the test is presented as the 
frequency of positive challenge results in test and control animals. 
Occasionally, the test group has a greater number of animals showing a response than 
the controls, although the intensity of the reaction is not greater than that observed on 
the controls.  In these instances, a re-challenge may be necessary to define the response 
clearly.  A re-challenge shall be carried out 1 to 2 weeks after the first challenge using 
the same animals. 
Note:  Background or artifactual reactions from fur clipping, patch edge, or nonspecific 
FCA effects were not considered as evidence of sensitization.

(Reference SOP: BIO-004) 
At least 34 guinea pigs of the same sex, will be used for this test and will be arbitrarily 
assigned to 4 groups (≥6 animals/control group, ≥11 animals/ test group).  All animals 
will be intradermally and topically inducted, and then received a challenge patch.  Score 
each challenge site approximately 24 h and 48 h following challenge. 
The observation will be conducted daily during the in-life phase.  The body weight will 
be collected at least once prior to the first dosing and once on the day of termination for 
all animals.

8.1 Dosing Procedures 
8.1.1 Induction I/Intradermal Induction Phase 
The dorsum will be prepared by removing the fur with an electric clipper prior 
to all steps in the test procedure. 
The first day of intraderma l induction dosing will be designated as Day 1.  
Formulations will be prepared for the control or test groups animals as indicated 
in  Table 8-1 and Figure 8-2.  The prepared formulations will be injected in 
pairs on each side of the dorsal midline.  Injections ‘a’ and ‘b’ will be given in 
close proximity to each othe r cranially; injection ‘c’ will be located caudally.   
Each injection site will be intradermally injected 0.1 mL. 
8.1.2 Induction II/Topical Induction Phase 
Approximately 24 ± 2 hours before topical induction administration, all the 
injection sites skin will be pai nted with about 0.5  mL/animal of 10%  sodium 
lauryl sulfate (SLS) in liquid paraffin.  If necessary, re-clip the dorsal test sites 
on all the test and control animals with a clipper, as necessary to expose the 
skin before SLS application.  Clean with diluted alcohol before SLS application.

report.  
17 EVALUTION CRITERIA 
After challenge or re -challenge dosing, grades of ‘1’ or greater in the test groups 
generally indicate sensitization, provided grades of less than ‘1’ are observed in the 
control animals.  If grades of ‘1’ or greater are noted in control animals, then the 
reactions of the test animals which exceed the most severe control reaction are presumed 
to be due to sensitization.  If the response is equivocal, re-challenge is recommended to 
confirm the results from the first challenge.  The outcome of the test is presented as the 
frequency of positive challenge results in test and control animals.

SUMMARY 
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the extract of a test article for cytotoxicity to 
mammalian cells in culture by a method compliant with the requirements specified in ISO 
10993-5:2009. 
The test article was extracted with 5% FBS complete MEM  medium in sterile vessels for 
72(±2) hours at 37℃ ±1℃ incubator with a ratio of 3 cm2/mL.  T he negative control article 
and positive control article were extracted with ratios of 3 cm2/mL and 6 cm2/mL respectively 
at the same conditions.  The vehicle control was extracted at the same conditions of test article. 
At the end of the extraction period, the maintenance culture medi um were removed from test 
culture wells and 2 mL extracts were added in triplicates.  Then the plates were incubated for 
about 72 hours in 37℃±1℃ carbon dioxide incubator with high humidity and CO2% set as 5%.  
The cultures were evaluated for cytotoxic effects by microscopic examination at time points of 
24 hours, 48 hours and 72 hours.  The cytotoxic response of all extracts was evaluated.  
The results showed that vehicle control and negative control  retained a healthy normal 
appearance throughout the duration of the test and displayed no cytotoxic reaction, scored “0”, 
and met the validat ion acceptance criteria.  Positive control displayed severe cytotoxic 
reaction, scored “4”, and met the acceptance criteria. 
Test article extract, displayed no reactivity with the same scores of “ 0”, at time points of 
24 hours, 48 hours, and 72 hours. 
Base on the above results, this MEM elution assay was considered valid and it was concluded 
that the test article was NON-CYTOTOXIC under the conditions of this study.

5.1 Cell Line 
The L -929 cells (ATCC cell line CCL -1) employed in this assay were mouse

L-929 cells were grown and used as monolayers in disposable tissue culture labware 
in a 37℃±1℃ carbon dioxide incubator with high humidity and CO2% set as 5% .  
The medium used for the growth of cells was minimal essential medium (MEM) 
supplemented with  10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).  The medium was also 
supplemented with the following: 2 mM L-glutamine, 100 units/mL penicillin, and 
100 µg/mL streptomycin.  The use of antibiotics in culture medium has not shown 
adverse effects when used for this assay. 
5.3 Justification for Selection of Test System 
The MEM elution assay is one of several in vitro mammalian cell tests which have 
been used to screen materials for their potential cytotoxicity.  The L -929 cell line 
has a history of use in assays of this type  and is recom mended in regulatory 
guidelines.

9 ASSAY EVALUATION 
(1) At the time points of 24, 48, and 72 hours, the plates were taken out and examined 
under 100× magnification microscope for signs of cytopathic effect.  Criteria for 
evaluating cytotoxicity included morphologic changes in cells, such as 
granulation, crenation, or rounding, and loss of viable cells from the monolayer 
by lysis or detachment. 
(2) A numerical score was assigned to each well using the following scale: 
Grade Reactivity Conditions of all Cultures 
0 None Discrete intracytoplasmic granules, no cell lysis, no reduction of cell growth 
1 Slight 
Not more than 20% of the cells are round, loosely attached, and 
without intracytoplasmic granules, or show changes in morphology; 
occasional lysed cells are present; only slight growth inhibition 
observable. 
2 Mild 
Not more than 50% of the cells are round, devoid of 
intracytoplasmic granules, no extensive cell lysis; not more than 
50% growth inhibition observable. 
3 Moderate 
Not more than 70% of the cell layers contain rounded cells or are 
lysed; cell layers not completely destroyed, but more than 50% 
growth inhibition observable. 
4 Severe Nearly complete or complete destruction of the cell layers. 
10 ASSAY VALIDITY 
Final evaluation of the validity of the assay and results were based upon the criteria 
listed below and scientific judgment. 
♦ The vehicle control s must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout the 
duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
♦ The negative controls must retain a healthy normal appearance throughout the 
duration of the test and must be scored “0”. 
♦ Positive control must display a moderate to severe cytotoxic reaction, displaying 
a score of ‘3’ or ‘4’ by final reading of the test. 
11 TEST ARTICLE EVALUATION CRITERIA 
Negative Response: 
Sample cultures scores of “0”, “1”, or, “2” on all scoring points, the sample is considered 
to be “NONTOXIC” and will be reported as “NON- CYTOTOXIC”. 
Positive Response: 
Sample cultures scores “3” on some or all scoring points, the sample is considered to be 
“MODERATELY TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”. 
Sample cultures displaying scores “4” at any of the scoring points, the sample is 
considered “TOXIC” and will be reported as “CYTOTOXIC”.

11 TEST SYSTEM 
11.1 Cell Line 
The L -929 cells (ATCC cell line CCL -1) employed in this assay are mouse 
fibroblasts, and sub-cultured in this laboratory.  Cell lines which are mycoplasma -
free are purchased from the vendor and are kept frozen in the lab until use. 
To maintain the sensitivity, they are only sub -cultured for up to 15 passages and 
then discarded.  If a stock culture of a cell line is stored, storage shall be  in liquid 
nitrogen (about -196℃).  If the cells are grown from cultures taken from storage, 
remove the cryoprotectant, if present.  Subculture the cells at least once before use. 
11.2 Medium and Cell Culture Condition 
L-929 cells are grown and used as monolayers in disposable tissue culture  labware 
in a 37 ℃ incubator with high humidity and CO 2% set as 5%  at WuXi AppTec.   
The incubator temperature range will be 37℃±1℃, any conditions exceeds the 
range and lasts longer than one hour will be recorded as a deviation.  The medium 
used for growth of cells is minimal essential medium (MEM) supplemented with 
5% (v/v) fetal bovine serum (FBS).  The medium is also supplemented with the 
following:  2 mM L -glutamine, 100 units/mL penicillin, and 100 µ g/mL 
streptomycin.  WuXi AppTec has a long-standing history using antibiotics in 
culture medium.  The use of antibiotics in culture media has not shown adverse 
effects when used for this assay.  This is exhibited in the varying degrees of 
toxicity seen in the assay controls 
11.3 Justification for Selection of Test System 
The MEM elution assay is one of several in vitro mammalian cell tests, which  
have been used to screen materials for their potential cytotoxicity.  The L-929 cell 
line has a history of use in assays of this type. 
12 PROCEDURES 
(BIO-047 and BIO-049) 
 L-929 cells will be plated at a sufficient seeding density for about 3 days before 
use.  Prior to dosing, the cell cultures will be examined to ensure they have 
formed a subconfluent monolayer (approximately 80% confluency) and that they 
appear uniform and viable.  
 2 mL aliquots of the test article and control article extracts will be plated in 
triplicate onto the cell line. 
 The cell cultures will be incubated in a humidified atmosphere for appropriately 
72 hours.  The monolayers will be evaluated for cytotoxi c effects at time points 
of 24, 48, and 72 hours .  At each incubation period the cell cultures will be 
observed for signs of cytopathic effect (CPE) including lysis, crenation, plaques, 
and excessive rounding of cells.
